title: Pocketcall: make a remote-controlled computer usable by a non-programmer
description: Pocketcall is a Claude Code plugin that makes a remote computer the person already pays for usable by a person who is not a programmer. It checks the seven things that silently decide whether a machine can be left working, including the shared folder a photo from town lands in, walks through the four minutes before leaving the house and the thirty seconds at the door, and answers as if someone is reading on a phone. On a work account it adds the company's own relay with an end-to-end encrypted approval card on the phone, and a voice note that becomes a task in the company's tracker, a pull request made by a cloud or home session, and a Yes from the phone that merges exactly the commit the card showed. No API keys asked for, no third-party sign-in.
